importance_ranking.reason: High visual sub-type variation — MS cabin, container kitchen, kiosk format, and trailer-mounted units are visually distinct. Buyers use the image to identify structure type before reading any text; wrong format is an immediate skip.

Kitchen size, structure material, and wall panel type are primary shortlisting criteria — they determine site fit, project compliance, and budget tier. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated by construction or industrial buyers.

Price varies substantially with size, structure material, and fit-out configuration — buyers discover and compare across spec tiers, not within a fixed tier. Indian B2B buyers are price-aggressive on capital purchases; listed price is a budget entry point before negotiation.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in the Indian portable kitchen market; buyers search by size, material, and price — not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Post-sale dependency is real — delivery, installation, and on-site commissioning require a capable manufacturer. Buyers evaluate fabrication track record and service reach after shortlisting on specs and price.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Custom-dimension builds may additionally quote per sq ft; rental deployments quote per month. However, the dominant transaction unit is per unit (one complete cabin/container) and is never a buyer question for standard purchases.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied for a complete prefabricated structure. No buyer questions whether a portable kitchen cabin is sold per unit.
